reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) comes from a single-phase CoCrFeNiMn HEA, not a dual-phase FCC/BCC coating, and attributes enhanced creep resistance to combined dynamic recrystallization and precipitation, not primarily to precipitates reinforcing phase boundaries. The key premise that precipitates act as barriers to dislocation climb at phase boundaries in an FCC/BCC system is not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: Dynamic nano-precipitates form in situ during continuous loading at intermediate temperatures in the FCC/BCC HEA coating.
These precipitates accumulate at grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
The precipitates act as barriers to stress-assisted dislocation climb in the FCC matrix.
This barrier effect raises the activation energy for dislocation motion and slows the creep rate.
Pre-treated coatings with promoted precipitation will show higher stress exponent, higher activation energy, and lower creep rate than quenched coatings.
